subject: FinVault continuity safeguard — RTO/RPO carveout request
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@finvault.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@finvault.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: FinVault continuity safeguards — multi-region RTO/RPO requirements

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — the performance looked good. As we move toward procurement, our security and ops teams surfaced two hard requirements for production:

- Multi-region failover with documented activation steps and test cadence.
- RTO target of 15 minutes for full service recovery when failing between EU regions, and RPO as close to 0 as possible for critical customer-facing traffic (payments, auth).

We understand some providers carve out liability for cross-region failover; FinVault needs explicit language describing the standby topology, activation lead time, and maximum permissible data loss for conditional liability.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these numbers, or alternatively propose a documented carveout we can review? I've attached our SLA questionnaire and a short list of scenarios the compliance team will use in their review.

Attachments: FinVault-SLA-questions.pdf

Thanks,
Emily Tran
Head of Security Operations
FinVault

Quick answers up front: we can support deterministic warm-standby topologies in the EU fleet, but the 15-minute RTO + zero-RPO across regions is a tight ask that depends on workload, request routing, and how you handle in-flight state. We should scope this as an exception / carveout in the contract with an explicit operational runbook and an agreed testing schedule.

Next steps:
- Karthik, can you review feasibility and a practical target (RTO/RPO) we can guarantee with warm standby and prefix/KV caching?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FinVault continuity safeguards — multi-region RTO/RPO requirements

Jonas / Grace — reviewed the questionnaire and ran a quick ops feasibility pass. Summary:

- Feasible topology: EU-primary (active) + EU-secondary (warm standby). We keep KV cache warm for critical prefixes and continuously replicate commit logs to standby.
- Recommended contractual targets: RTO = 30 minutes (activation + cache rebuild) for full service recovery; RPO = <= 30 seconds for traffic routed through our managed gateways when using our prefix-caching + WAL replication option.
- Why not 15m/0s: cross-region network uncertainty and write-ack behavior mean you can't guarantee absolute zero loss at scale without synchronous cross-region writes (which have large latency and cost implications). We can, however, offer near-zero under specific configurations (sync writes to two replicas inside EU) — this adds both cost and per-request latency.

Operational items to include in an SLA carveout:
- Warm standby activation lead time and responsible parties.
- Test cadence (quarterly DR drills + one full failover/year) and pass/fail criteria.
- Capacity delta estimate (how much reserved capacity to keep in standby). See attached delta estimate spreadsheet.
- A liability cap for data-loss windows tied to the chosen replication mode.

I attached the redwood-warm-standby-delta-estimate.xlsx with a sample sizing for FinVault's 95th-percentile transaction load. If they want 15m/0s we can model synchronous cross-region replication but will call out the expected latency hit and cost uplift.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-warm-standby-delta-estimate.xlsx

Emily / Marcus — thanks for your patience while we scoped this. Based on Karthik's ops pass, here's a concrete, testable amendment proposal you can take to procurement/security:

Proposal (high level):
- Topology: EU active + EU warm standby with continuous WAL replication for critical prefixes. Standby kept at reserved capacity (sizing in attached spreadsheet).
- Contractual targets: RTO = 30 minutes (from declared switchover start to all production routes restored); RPO = <= 30 seconds for calls that go through Redwood-managed gateways when using the recommended replication mode.
- Optional synchronous replication mode: can be enabled for up to 3 critical services to achieve near-zero RPO; this will increase per-request latency and cost — see delta estimate.
- Tests & governance: quarterly DR drills led jointly; one full failover test per 12 months; activation runbook stored in the shared runbook link below.
- Liability carveout: Redwood will assume liability up to an agreed cap for data loss windows tied to chosen replication mode; we will provide explicit wording for DocuSign review.

Attachments: SLA-draft-FinVault-v1.docx (contains suggested contract language), redwood-warm-standby-delta-estimate.xlsx

If that direction is acceptable, I'll open a DocuSign for the amendment and a HubSpot task for procurement to review the costs. Proposed quick call to finalize language: Monday 21 Jun, 10:00–10:30am UTC?
